answer: Time-lock the history and cap the payout per identity per epoch, so no single key can out-earn its share by volume. Example: an identity with 40 submissions in one epoch is paid for 10, which removes the incentive to flood and makes a farm's throughput irrelevant. Auditors rotate from a pool, so a bought seat has a shelf life of 4 epochs. Clever designs usually fail here, because the cap also caps honest high-volume operators, and that is the trade. A kernel of 10 paid answers per epoch is the ridge the economy sits on, and the inlet of new keys gets no special path.
